A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 55-page CDAS study, including complete appendices A–K. Text and rendering comparisons establish that pages 2–55 are identical; page 1 differs only in author information and the arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original CDAS experiments on AXBENCH, refusal steering, and backdoor neutralization in Sections 4–5, with additional original ablations and analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experimental results, including Tables 1–4, Figure 1, and the appendix ablations and analyses.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same rank-1 CDAS method, distributed interchange interventions, Jensen–Shannon distribution-matching objective, and clamping inference procedure. The method appendices are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same AXBENCH/CONCEPT500 coverage, refusal and backdoor scenarios, utility benchmarks, and appendix datasets. No task, population, or test scenario changes.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods: Prompt, LoReFT, RePS, BiPO, Lang., and DIM in Table 1; DAS, RePS, and DIM in the case studies; and RePS with DII in the appendix ablations.

E3.justification: Model and layer configurations, sample sizes, data splits, factor searches, evaluation metrics, and testing procedures are identical in Sections 4–5 and Appendices G–I.

E4.justification: The objective comparison in Appendix E.2, failure analysis in G.4, ablations in G.5 and H.7, continual-fine-tuning analysis in I.6, and mechanistic analysis in J are all unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same ten random splits for AXBENCH fair scores, three random initializations for backdoor results, standard-error shading in Figure 1, and appendix seed information.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative findings match, including the CDAS score of 0.992 for Gemma-2-9B at layer 20 in Table 1 and true-trigger ASR of 6.68% in Figure 1. Appendix result entries are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and objectives in Section 3, formulas and computational-cost derivation in Appendix D, and first-order-effect definition in Appendix J are identical. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and conditional claims about CDAS, model scale, steering effectiveness, and utility preservation.

C2.justification: Interpretations of scale and layer sensitivity, overfitting, and utility preservation are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning training data, factor tuning, rank-1 interventions, and causal grounding.

D1.justification: Hardware information, implementation settings, hyperparameters, data preparation, and reproducibility statements remain identical. The author email update does not alter the stated code or data access arrangements.

R1.justification: Section 2, the references, and appendix citations are unchanged, as is the positioning relative to DAS, preference optimization, and other steering approaches.

P1.justification: Page 1 adds affiliation 2, Ningbo Global Innovation Center, to Jintao Chen and changes his email from jintaochen@zju.edu.cn to chenjintao@zju.edu.cn. The arXiv version/date stamp updates; the body text and document structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, captions, numbering, and placement are unchanged. Pages 2–55 render identically, and page 1 retains its layout despite the author-information and stamp edits.

improvement.justification: v2 updates author affiliation/contact information and the arXiv stamp, while retaining identical scientific content, evidence, explanations, limitations, and appendix material. These administrative edits do not meaningfully change the paper's overall quality.
